questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write polite emails
What politeness is and why we teach it to children
Why British people are ruder than before
How to remember people's names
questions.why: They discuss whether a boy was impolite and why we teach kids to be polite.

questions.q: Why does Beth say 'You, give me that pen!' at the start?
options: Because she is angry with Neil
Because Neil took her pen
To give an example of asking for something rudely
To show a typical, polite British way of asking for something
questions.why: Neil says it was a bit rude, and they then practise the polite version.

questions.q: Why did the boy call Michael Rosen 'thingy'?
options: He recognised him but couldn't remember his name
He wanted to insult him
He thought Michael was someone else he had seen on television
It is Michael's nickname
questions.why: Beth says the boy recognised Michael but couldn't remember his name.

questions.q: Why did the boy's words give Michael Rosen a problem?
options: He didn't understand what the boy meant by the word 'innit'
The boy was very aggressive
He was in a hurry
They broke the usual rules, so he didn't know how to reply
questions.why: He says it broke all the rules, 'it gave me a problem. How do I answer it?'

questions.q: What does Professor Louise Mullany think is the key to whether something is polite?
options: How old the speaker is
Whether the speaker uses formal words and a polite tone of voice
Whether the speaker says 'please'
How the person being spoken to understands it
questions.why: She says 'the crucial thing there is in how you've perceived it'.

questions.q: How did Michael Rosen feel about the boy?
options: He felt friendly towards him and didn't think he was rude
He felt insulted and upset
He was frightened of him
He wanted to correct the boy's English and teach him better manners
questions.why: Louise says he didn't see it as insulting and was 'quite kindly disposed' to the boy.

questions.q: According to Louise, why do we teach children to be polite?
options: So they get better marks at school and pass their exams
So they make adults laugh
So they can be accepted in society
So they can speak more formally
questions.why: She thinks teaching politeness helps children enjoy the benefits of being accepted in society.

questions.q: How did Louise feel when her daughter wouldn't say hello to the nursery cook?
options: Proud that her daughter was so independent and confident
Very embarrassed, so she made excuses for her
Angry with the cook
Not worried, because she was only two
questions.why: She says 'the embarrassment was so strong' and she made excuses like 'she's tired'.
